Figure 13.13 Figure associated with Examples 13.7 and 13.8. (left column) The sigmoid function (top panel) and its derivative (bottom panel). The derivative here maps most input values away from the origin to output near zero, which can cause the gradient of a network employing sigmoid activation to vanish during optimization and thus prevent adequate parameter tuning. (right column) The ReLU function (top panel) and its derivative (bottom panel). While not as susceptible to vanishing gradient problems, networks employing the ReLU need to be initialized away from zero to prevent units from disappearing. See text for further details.
